bibl.title: Priming of Control: Implicit Contextual Cuing of Top-down Attentional Set

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: These results suggest that top-down control states can be bound into episodic event representations and can subsequently be primed by other features of those representations.

span.label: context-specific improvements in interference resolution (priming of control)
span.quote: We used fMRI to test the priming of control hypothesis, the proposition that implicit contextual cues can trigger bottom-up retrieval of specific top-down control settings.

span.label: fmri
span.quote: Here, we harnessed functional magnetic resonance imaging in humans to test whether these behavioral findings truly reflect online, bottom-up priming of top-down attentional control settings.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Top-down control settings are bound into episodic event-file representations, so that later presentation of another feature of that representation (the contextual cue) implicitly retrieves and reinstates the control setting.
span.quote: we propose that top-down control settings associated with specific contextual information can be bound into episodic “event file” representations, and that, subsequently, their retrieval can be implicitly primed by other features of that representation

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Experienced conflict triggers an arousal/noradrenergic response which, via Hebbian associative learning, binds the current bottom-up context representation to the top-down task/biasing representation.
span.quote: According to the model, the experience of conflict elicits an arousal response (accompanied by noradrenalin release) that in turn promotes the binding of current bottom-up stimulus/context representations and top-down task representations/biasing processes via Hebbian (associative) learning

span.label: The functional profile of mSPL was only sampled at two conflict-frequency levels and would need parametric variation of cues or load to be characterised properly.
span.quote: Future studies could potentially delineate the functional characteristics of this region more systematically by varying attentional cues or load in a more continuous, parametric fashion.

span.label: How the reduced FFA lateralisation in the high-conflict context actually produces the behavioural benefit is not established.
span.quote: Although this finding echoes recent reports of spatially global gain modulation under conditions of increased cognitive control ( Ester et al., 2009 ; King et al., 2010 ), the precise mechanisms by which this bilateral recruitment of the FFA for stimuli presented in the high-conflict hemifield translated into context-specific improvements in interference resolution remain unclear.

span.label: dichotomy
span.quote: Recent behavioral findings, however, suggest that this juxtaposition of automatic and controlled processing may in fact represent a false dichotomy

span.label: contextual cues
span.quote: However, recent behavioral studies have cast doubt on the validity of this dichotomy, showing that implicit contextual cues can modulate performance in a way suggestive of an associative triggering of specific top-down control states

span.label: top-down control
span.quote: However, recent behavioral studies have cast doubt on the validity of this dichotomy, showing that implicit contextual cues can modulate performance in a way suggestive of an associative triggering of specific top-down control states

span.label: interference resolution
span.quote: Using a flanker interference task where stimulus location cued the likelihood of incongruent trials, we found that the behavioral phenomenon of implicit, context-specific improvements in interference resolution was mirrored in hemodynamic activity in the medial superior parietal lobule

span.label: A FALSE DICHOTOMY, NAMED AS SUCH: `Recent behavioral findings, however, suggest that this juxtaposition of automatic and controlled processing may in fact represent A FALSE DICHOTOMY.` The distinction between bottom-up association and deliberate top-down control is the oldest working partition in this literature, and the paper's contribution is to show a case that sits on both sides of it - an ASSOCIATIVE trigger for a CONTROL state
span.quote: Recent behavioral findings, however, suggest that this juxtaposition of automatic and controlled processing may in fact represent a false dichotomy

span.label: PRIMING APPLIED TO A CONTROL SETTING - a fifth kind of thing for the word in this corpus, beside a concept, a behaviour, a goal and a sentence structure. `Top-down control states can be BOUND INTO EPISODIC EVENT REPRESENTATIONS and can subsequently be PRIMED by other features of those representations.` The claim is that a control configuration is storable and retrievable like any other feature of an episode, so the machinery already built for priming concepts applies to it unchanged
span.quote: These results suggest that top-down control states can be bound into episodic event representations and can subsequently be primed by other features of those representations

span.label: THE MIRROR OF Kiefer2012, tagged earlier tonight. Kiefer argued that top-down configuration GATES unconscious processing - control reaching down into the automatic. This paper argues the other direction: an automatic associative cue TRIGGERS a control state. Between them the boundary is crossed both ways, and neither needs the other to be wrong. What is left of `automatic` after both is the pair of criteria Kiefer kept - not conscious, not deliberately initiated - and nothing about autonomy
span.quote: However, recent behavioral studies have cast doubt on the validity of this dichotomy, showing that implicit contextual cues can modulate performance in a way suggestive of an associative triggering of specific top-down control states

span.label: AWARENESS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, AND THE CONCLUSION IS DEFINITIONAL: the effect occurred `despite the participant's lack of awareness of systematic variation in conflict frequency, illustrating the implicit nature of the phenomenon and delivering further evidence QUESTIONING THE NOTION THAT CONTROLLED PROCESSING IS INHERENTLY VOLITIONAL`. A survey after scanning quantified what participants noticed. The target is not a finding but a property the word `controlled` is usually taken to carry
span.quote: Crucially, this “pure” expression of contextual conflict-control occurred despite the participant's lack of awareness of systematic variation in conflict frequency, illustrating the implicit nature of the phenomenon and delivering further evidence questioning the notion that controlled processing is inherently volitional

span.label: extends → Vandenberghe et al., 2001; Yantis et al., 2002; Serences et al., 2004; Shulman et al., 2009
span.quote: These findings extend the established role of the mSPL in mediating explicitly cued shifts of attention ( Vandenberghe et al., 2001 ; Yantis et al., 2002 ; Serences et al., 2004 ; Shulman et al., 2009 ) to include the retrieval and execution of implicitly primed control settings.

span.label: replicates → Crump et al., 2006
span.quote: Furthermore, contrary to the suspicion that that this phenomenon merely reflects aggregate congruency sequence effects, context-specific improvements in interference resolution were dissociable from such trial-by-trial “conflict adaptation” effects in the current study, verifying previous reports ( Crump et al., 2006 ).

span.label: contextual cues —causes→ top-down control
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE PAPER'S CLAIM, and the direction is the surprising half: the ASSOCIATIVE process is the cause and the CONTROL state is the effect, which is the reverse of how the dichotomy arranges them. `suggestive of` is the hedge in this span - the fMRI result is what upgrades it, and that is a separate edge.
span.quote: However, recent behavioral studies have cast doubt on the validity of this dichotomy, showing that implicit contextual cues can modulate performance in a way suggestive of an associative triggering of specific top-down control states

span.label: contextual cues —causes→ interference resolution
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — The behavioural expression, and the paper's own summary sentence. `support the proposal` is its strength - this is an fMRI study confirming and localising a behavioural phenomenon rather than establishing it.
span.quote: However, recent behavioral studies have cast doubt on the validity of this dichotomy, showing that implicit contextual cues can modulate performance in a way suggestive of an associative triggering of specific top-down control states. Here, we harnessed functional magnetic resonance imaging in humans to test whether these behavioral findings truly reflect online, bottom-up priming of top-down attentional control settings. Using a flanker interference task where stimulus location cued the likelihood of incongruent trials, we found that the behavioral phenomenon of implicit, context-specific improvements in interference resolution

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Our primary analyses tested for contextual variation in interference effects (incongruent − congruent) in mean reaction times (RT) on correct trials (excluding posterror trials) and error rates with 2 (context: high-conflict vs low-conflict) × 2 (congruency: congruent vs incongruent) repeated-measures ANOVAs.

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Statistical parametric maps (SPMs) of cortical sensitivity to face stimuli (face > house + scrambled images) and stimulus location (left > right stimulation side and right > left stimulation) were calculated for each subject and entered into voxelwise one-sample t tests

span.label: regression
span.quote: we entered each participant's context × congruency interaction SPM into a second-level random effect group regression analysis

span.label: binomial test
span.quote: 17 individuals correctly reported which side of the display had a greater proportion of incongruent trials in their version of the experiment, while only 8 answered incorrectly (binomial test; p = 0.054)

span.label: correlation
span.quote: the magnitude of contextual lateralization reduction in the FFA (lateralization low-conflict context − lateralization high-conflict context ) correlated with the degree of contextual interference reduction in behavior

span.label: Monte Carlo simulation
span.quote: the program was used to run 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations taking into account the whole-brain search volume and the estimated smoothness of each axis of the respective group SPMs

span.label: maximum likelihood estimation
span.quote: Temporal autocorrelations were estimated using restricted maximum likelihood estimates of variance components with a first-order autoregressive model

span.label: Interference (flanker congruency) effects in reaction time were smaller for stimuli appearing in the location associated with frequent conflict than in the low-conflict location.
span.quote: interference effects were reduced for stimuli presented in the high-conflict location (94 ms) relative to those in the low-conflict context (123 ms; F (1,24) = 7.6; p = 0.01

span.label: Two regions, left dorsal premotor cortex and right medial superior parietal lobule, showed the context-by-congruency interaction in hemodynamic activity.
span.quote: Two regions emerged displaying differential patterns of conflict processing for stimuli presented in the high- versus low-conflict context: the left dorsal premotor cortex and the right medial superior parietal lobule

span.label: The mSPL showed context-specific functional coupling with visual cortex and fusiform face area regions, indicating top-down biasing of sensory processing.
span.quote: In line with a role of the mSPL in contextual conflict-control, BOLD activity in this region associated with differential conflict processing in the high- versus low-conflict context significantly covaried with that in both visual cortex ROIs

span.label: Contextual control was implemented online rather than as a sustained attentional set: the behavioural benefit was absent on the first trial after a switch into the high-conflict context and present only on repetitions.
span.quote: The three-way interaction was significant ( F (1,24) = 10.9; p < 0.005), such that reduced interference effects were not evident following a transition from the low- to high-conflict context

span.label: Participants were essentially unaware of the location-based conflict-frequency manipulation, establishing that the effect is implicit.
span.quote: only one of 25 participants in the current experiment reported noticing the location-based manipulation of conflict frequency in our post-test survey

span.label: Stimulus-driven lateralization in the fusiform face area was abolished in the high-conflict context, consistent with spatially global gain modulation under elevated control.
span.quote: while lateralization was present in the FFA for stimuli presented in the low-conflict context ( t (24) = 3.0; p < 0.01), it was absent for stimuli presented in the high-conflict context

span.label: Individual differences in the FFA lateralization reduction tracked individual differences in the behavioural interference reduction.
span.quote: the magnitude of contextual lateralization reduction in the FFA (lateralization low-conflict context − lateralization high-conflict context ) correlated with the degree of contextual interference reduction in behavior

span.label: priming of control
span.quote: This has raised the intriguing prospect of “priming of control,” the possibility that top-down control may be subject to associative bottom-up retrieval, triggered by stimulus context

span.label: psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analysis
span.quote: Psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analysis provides a measure of functional connectivity by quantifying covariation of activation time courses between different brain regions

span.label: conflict-frequency context (high- vs low-conflict stimulus location)
span.term: conflict-frequency context (high- vs low-conflict stimulus location)
span.quote: Conflict frequency was manipulated according to stimulus location by defining one side of fixation as a high-conflict context (25% congruent/75% incongruent trials) and the other as a low-conflict context

span.label: flanker congruency (congruent vs incongruent)
span.quote: Target and flanker face viewpoint direction was congruent in half of all trials and incongruent in the other.

span.label: context transition (repetition vs switch)
span.quote: we reanalyzed the RT data with 2 (context transition: repetition vs switch) × 2 (context) × 2 (congruency) ANOVAs

span.label: reaction time and error rate (interference effect)
span.term: reaction time and error rate (interference effect)
span.quote: Our primary analyses tested for contextual variation in interference effects (incongruent − congruent) in mean reaction times (RT) on correct trials (excluding posterror trials) and error rates with 2 (context: high-conflict vs low-conflict) × 2 (congruency: congruent vs incongruent) repeated-measures ANOVAs.

span.label: individual mean reaction time (overall response speed)
span.term: individual mean reaction time (overall response speed)
span.quote: and, to control for between-subject variability in overall response speed, individual mean RT as covariates

span.label: 94 ms vs 123 ms — size of the flanker interference effect in the high-conflict versus low-conflict location
span.quote: interference effects were reduced for stimuli presented in the high-conflict location (94 ms) relative to those in the low-conflict context (123 ms; F (1,24) = 7.6; p = 0.01

span.label: 25 — number of participants retained for analysis after exclusions
span.quote: The remaining 25 participants were 14 females and 11 males (mean age = 23.8 years; range = 18–33 years).

span.label: 93% — overall accuracy on the flanker task
span.quote: Overall performance of the flanker task was high (93% correct) and characterized by typical interference effects.

span.label: 783 ms vs 674 ms — mean reaction time on incongruent versus congruent trials
span.quote: RTs were slower for incongruent stimuli (783 ms) than for congruent arrays (674 ms; F (1,24) = 133.8; p < 0.0001).

span.label: p = 0.054 — binomial test on the 17-vs-8 split of participants correctly forced-choosing the high-conflict side, taken as evidence of implicit knowledge
span.quote: 17 individuals correctly reported which side of the display had a greater proportion of incongruent trials in their version of the experiment, while only 8 answered incorrectly (binomial test; p = 0.054)

span.label: 25% congruent/75% incongruent — the conflict-frequency ratio defining the high-conflict context (reversed for the low-conflict context)
span.quote: Conflict frequency was manipulated according to stimulus location by defining one side of fixation as a high-conflict context (25% congruent/75% incongruent trials) and the other as a low-conflict context
